clips.prompt:
Animate this exact illustration; the first and last frames are the same provided frame and must be matched exactly, so the clip loops seamlessly. Subject continuity: the same carved marble hand reaching from the left across a halftone dissolve and a deep red circle; the bent index fingertip rests on top of a small brushed-metal knob and the thumb tip on its lower left, pinching it; the knob is set in a dark ring on a dark panel; the hand has exactly five fingers.
Motion beats: 0–0.5 s: the index fingertip and thumb tip tighten their pinch on the knob rim. 0.5–2.0 s: keeping the pinch, the wrist and hand rotate clockwise about 25 degrees around the knob's centre, as if slowly turning up a volume dial: the index fingertip rolls down and to the right along the top of the rim, the thumb tip rolls up and to the left along the bottom of the rim; the knuckles and the back of the hand follow slightly. 2.0–2.4 s: the pinch relaxes, both fingertips still touching the rim. 2.4–3.6 s: the fingertips slide back along the rim, counter-clockwise, to their starting places while the knob stays still. 3.6–4.0 s: the hand settles into exactly the starting pinch — the provided last frame.
Hard constraints: the index fingertip and the thumb tip touch the knob rim for the entire clip; they never lift off, never leave the knob and never point away from it. The index finger stays bent over the knob the whole time; it never straightens, extends or slides off. Only the hand and fingers move, by a small amount; the forearm stays almost still and the hand stays one continuous limb. The knob, its dark ring, the dark panel, the red circle and the cream ground never move, grow or change. No second hand, no new objects.
Locked-off camera: no zoom, no pan, no tilt, no dolly, no shake; framing and scale identical to the provided frame.
Lighting continuity: the same soft key light from the upper left; no flicker, no exposure change.
Background: the provided strip colours stay perfectly flat (cream left, deep red circle, near-black panel right); the repeated rows above and below the strip are static padding and never move.
Materials: the hand stays carved warm-ivory marble with fine tan veining (no skin, no flesh tones). The square-dot halftone pattern is a fixed printed texture: every square stays exactly in place and at the same density — it does not fade, flicker, crawl or disappear.
End: the clip settles exactly on the provided last frame.
Avoid: text, letters, logos, watermark, new objects, extra hands or fingers, deformed hands, fingers lifting off the knob, pointing finger, camera motion, background change, halftone changes, morphing, cuts, the knob moving or changing size. Silent.

promptRules.source: Lessons from the approved hero D draft (revision 3 prompts).
rules: Loops are 4 s unless the beats need more (career removals 6 s: lift, carry out of frame and return the empty hand; products-reader 6 s: two blinks in 4 s read as twitching).
Every prompt carries a "Hard constraints" line: what must not move, where the gaze stays, max head rotation (~3–5°), hands stay in place, explicit no chin-lift / no upward glance.
The halftone is described as a fixed printed texture that never fades, flickers or crawls.
Loops use first = last frame; one-shot clips end and hold on the provided last frame.
The "Avoid:" list is part of the prompt text (the API ignores a separate negative prompt).
Every take is post-processed with scripts/roman-v2-motion-post.mjs (locked-background cinemagraph) and cropped with cropToPage.
No hex colour codes in prompt text — Veo can render them as on-screen text (jj-idle-desktop-t2 drew "#59112"); name colours in words.

Hand removals: the hand and forearm stay one continuous limb and return along the same path; nothing is left behind where the hand was (round-1 drafts left an empty sleeve and popped the hand back in).
